title: Python SDK: add batching_tier to examples + docstring references (no API break)
author: Monica Patel
description: Summary: This PR updates the Python SDK examples to show how to set the new tiered batching default via `batching_tier` (fast/standard/cost_efficient), and adds lightweight docstring references so users can discover the knobs without digging through release notes. This is intentionally no-breaking-change: the new parameter is optional, request serialization is backwards-compatible, and existing explicit batching overrides (when present) still behave as before. Motivation/Context: As part of Workload-aware batching defaults (Cost Optimization Automation), we’re introducing tiered defaults in the runtime/config layer. SDK examples need to be updated so customers can opt in during beta and understand the trade-offs. This PR focuses on examples + docstrings only; it does not change endpoint behavior or defaults. User-facing behavior: - Users can pass `batching_tier="fast" | "standard" | "cost_efficient"` in example code for Chat/Completions routes. - If users don’t pass it, behavior is unchanged. - Docstrings include a short note and link target (docs slug) so the tier feature is discoverable. Notes: - We use `cost_efficient` (underscored) to match the runtime/config spelling. - Examples avoid suggesting tier changes for streaming unless explicitly called out (fast tier recommended for token cadence). Checklist: - [x] Update examples (chat + completions) - [x] Add docstrings note for tier + precedence (tier defaults vs explicit overrides) - [x] Add simple serialization test for the new field - [x] Keep backwards compatibility - [x] Run formatting/lint (ruff/black) and unit tests Related: Linear ENG-18426 (SDK examples), PM-413 (tier naming/contracts).
commits: examples: add batching_tier to chat + completions snippets
docsstrings: mention batching_tier + precedence and link to docs
tests: assert request serialization includes batching_tier when provided
chore: ruff formatting + small example cleanup
changed_areas: redwood_ai/ (type hints / request models docstring touchups)
review_conversation: Alex Martinez (review): Can we add one explicit note in the example comments about streaming? We’ve seen customers flip cost-efficient on streaming routes and then report cadence regressions. Even if runtime is improving, the example should steer them to fast tier for streaming unless they know what they’re doing.
Monica Patel (author): Good call. I’ll add a short comment above the streaming example block: recommend `fast` for streaming-first UX; point to docs for trade-offs.

Wei Chen (review): Docstring link should be stable. Do we have an agreed docs slug yet? If not, can we keep it generic (e.g., “See: Batching profiles”) without hardcoding a URL that might change before GA.

Monica Patel (author): Updated to reference the docs section name ("Batching profiles") and kept the URL behind our docs shortlink format. If the slug changes, the redirect should hold. Also added a TODO tag so we can revisit at GA.

Nikhil Sharma (review): Naming: confirm `cost_efficient` vs `cost-efficient`. The runtime config I’ve seen is underscored, but Console copy uses hyphen. Please ensure request field is underscored and examples use the same string.

Monica Patel (author): Confirmed: request field uses `cost_efficient`. Updated examples and test accordingly; docstrings mention that UI may display “Cost-efficient” but API value is `cost_efficient`.
Elliot Price (review): Can we mention precedence briefly (explicit batching knobs override tier)? We keep getting support questions about “why didn’t tier change anything?”

Monica Patel (author): Added a one-liner in docstrings + examples README: “Tier sets defaults; explicit overrides take precedence.” Linked to the config explainability endpoint mention (no details) so users know where to look in Console.
Alex Martinez (approval): Looks good after the streaming guidance comment. Approved.
Wei Chen (approval): Approved. Docstring wording is clear and not overly promissory.
Nikhil Sharma (approval): Approved. Thanks for aligning API spelling.
Monica Patel (author): Merging after CI green.
release_notes: Python SDK examples now demonstrate optional `batching_tier` usage (fast/standard/cost_efficient) for workload-aware batching defaults; docstrings include brief guidance and precedence notes. No breaking changes.
